readings.heading: Ὁ Ἀπόστολος — 1 Corinthians 15:12–19
verses: 12. Brothers and sisters: if Christ is preached as raised from the dead, how can some of you say there is no resurrection of the dead?
13. But if there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ has not been raised either.
14. And if Christ has not been raised, then our preaching is empty — and your faith is empty too.
15. And we turn out to be false witnesses about God, because we testified against God that he raised the Christ — whom he did not raise, if it is really true that the dead are not raised.
16. Because if the dead are not raised, then Christ has not been raised either.
17. And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile — you are still in your sins.
18. In that case, those who have fallen asleep in Christ are lost as well.
19. If in this life we have hope in Christ and nothing more, we are the most pitiable of all people.

readings.heading: Τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον — Matthew 21:18–22
verses: 18. At that time, early in the morning, as Jesus was going back up to the city, he was hungry.

19. And seeing a single fig tree by the road, he went up to it and found nothing on it but leaves only. And he says to it: "May no fruit ever come from you again." And the fig tree withered on the spot.
20. And seeing it, the disciples marvelled, saying: "How did the fig tree wither on the spot?"

21. Jesus answered and said to them: "I tell you the truth: if you have faith and do not waver, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree — even if you say to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' it will happen.
22. And everything you ask for in prayer, believing, you will receive."
